clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 10346 state the order's subject (preparation of civil defense emergency plans by Federal agencies) and the authority under which the President acted, the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950; they operate only through the numbered sections that follow. It ended when EO 11490 of October 28, 1969 revoked the order: Sec. 3015 of that order states "The following are hereby revoked:" and item (4) of the list is EO 10346 of April 17, 1952. No earlier end is shown: the only instruments in the chain for this order are EO 11051 (an amendment of agency references) and EO 11490 (the revocation), and the held texts that cite this order by number (EO 10438, EO 10529, EO 10773, EO 11051) amend or refer to it without revoking it.

Section 1 of EO 10346 directs each Federal department and agency, in consultation with the Federal Civil Defense Administration, to prepare plans for providing its personnel, materials, facilities and services under section 302 of the Federal Civil Defense Act during a civil-defense emergency, taking into account the essential military requirements of the Department of Defense. It was a continuing planning duty. It ended when EO 11490 of October 28, 1969 revoked the order: Sec. 3015 of that order states "The following are hereby revoked:" and item (4) of the list is EO 10346 of April 17, 1952. No earlier end is shown: the only instruments in the chain for this order are EO 11051 (an amendment of agency references) and EO 11490 (the revocation), and the held texts that cite this order by number (EO 10438, EO 10529, EO 10773, EO 11051) amend or refer to it without revoking it.

Section 2 of EO 10346 directs each department and agency to prepare plans for maintaining the continuity of its essential functions during a civil-defense emergency, gives the National Security Resources Board authority to set uniform standards for them, and makes the portion of a plan concerning functions at the seat of Government effective on approval by the President. It was a continuing duty. EO 10438 (signed 1953-03-13) transferred to the Director of Defense Mobilization the functions vested in the National Security Resources Board and its Chairman by this order and amended the order accordingly, and EO 11051 (signed 1962-09-27) substituted agency references in the order; both are amendments that left the section in force. It ended when EO 11490 of October 28, 1969 revoked the order: Sec. 3015 of that order states "The following are hereby revoked:" and item (4) of the list is EO 10346 of April 17, 1952. No earlier end is shown: the only instruments in the chain for this order are EO 11051 (an amendment of agency references) and EO 11490 (the revocation), and the held texts that cite this order by number (EO 10438, EO 10529, EO 10773, EO 11051) amend or refer to it without revoking it.

Section 3 of EO 10346 directs the Federal Civil Defense Administrator to assist departments and agencies by indicating the types of personnel, materials, facilities and services useful for civil-defense purposes, to arrange for use of those not needed for continuity of essential functions, and to coordinate the arrangements with national, State and local civil-defense plans. It was a continuing duty. It ended when EO 11490 of October 28, 1969 revoked the order: Sec. 3015 of that order states "The following are hereby revoked:" and item (4) of the list is EO 10346 of April 17, 1952. No earlier end is shown: the only instruments in the chain for this order are EO 11051 (an amendment of agency references) and EO 11490 (the revocation), and the held texts that cite this order by number (EO 10438, EO 10529, EO 10773, EO 11051) amend or refer to it without revoking it.

research_rationale:
EO 10346 (1952-04-17; Preparation by Federal Agencies of Civil Defense Emergency Plans) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (17 FR 3477-3478), whose file also contains neighbouring orders; the order was delimited by its heading and the Harry S. Truman signature line, and the dossier's machine inventory, which spans text of other orders, was replaced with the four scopes below. Its own terms contain no end date or end condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, read in the Federal Register text of 34 FR 17567 onward. EO 10438 and EO 11051 are recorded as amendments on Section 2. EO 10773 (which restates references to the Federal Civil Defense Administrator in this and other orders) and EO 10529 (which cites Section 3 of this order) were read as leads and are not recorded as events or ends; I did not establish an effective date for the EO 10773 reference change, so it is not claimed.
